subject: HEALTH
title: Health & Wellness
description: A one-year high school health course aligned to the 2008 California Health Education Content Standards and the 2019 Health Education Framework. Students build the eight health skills (accessing information, analyzing influences, communication, decision making, goal setting, self-management and advocacy) while studying nutrition and physical activity, mental and emotional health, alcohol, tobacco and other drugs (including fentanyl and naloxone), injury and violence prevention, and personal and community health. Unit 5 (weeks 19–25) delivers comprehensive sexual health and HIV prevention education under the California Healthy Youth Act (Ed. Code 51930–51939); parents/guardians may review materials and opt the student out in writing, in which case the student completes an alternate health research project for those weeks.
framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grades 9–12); 2019 CA Health Education Framework; California Healthy Youth Act (Ed. Code 51930–51939)

standards.H-HS.1.1.P: Explain the interrelationships of physical, mental/emotional, and social health across the lifespan (wellness).
standards.H-HS.1.2.P: Describe how communicable diseases are transmitted and prevented, including hand hygiene and immunization.
standards.H-HS.1.3.P: Explain risk factors for and prevention of chronic diseases such as heart disease, diabetes, and cancer.
standards.H-HS.1.4.P: Describe personal health practices including sleep, dental, vision, hearing, and sun protection.
standards.H-HS.1.6.P: Explain how environmental factors such as air quality and water affect personal and community health.
standards.H-HS.2.1.P: Evaluate health products, services, and advertising claims as an informed consumer.
standards.H-HS.3.1.P: Access valid health information, products, and services, including health care providers and coverage options.
standards.H-HS.5.1.P: Use a decision-making process to make health-enhancing choices about personal and community health.
standards.H-HS.6.1.P: Set a personal wellness goal, develop an action plan, and monitor progress.
standards.H-HS.7.1.P: Practice behaviors that prevent disease, such as self-exams, sleep routines, and hygiene.
standards.H-HS.8.1.P: Advocate for a personal, family, or community health issue using accurate information.
standards.H-HS.1.1.N: Explain the relationship between nutrition, physical activity, and health, and interpret food labels.
standards.H-HS.1.2.N: Describe the functions and sources of macronutrients, micronutrients, and water, and the Dietary Guidelines/MyPlate recommendations.
standards.H-HS.1.3.N: Explain energy balance and healthy weight management, and the risks of eating disorders and unsafe weight-control practices.
standards.H-HS.1.4.N: Describe safe food handling and the prevention of foodborne illness.
standards.H-HS.1.5.N: Explain the benefits of regular physical activity and the components of health-related fitness.
standards.H-HS.2.1.N: Analyze how media, culture, and marketing influence food choices and body image.
standards.H-HS.3.1.N: Evaluate the validity of nutrition information and dietary supplement claims.
standards.H-HS.6.1.N: Develop a personal plan for healthy eating and physical activity.
standards.H-HS.7.1.N: Plan and prepare healthy, affordable meals and snacks.
standards.H-HS.1.1.M: Describe characteristics of mental and emotional wellness, including self-esteem, resilience, and emotional regulation.
standards.H-HS.1.2.M: Describe the signs, symptoms, and treatment of common mental health conditions, including depression and anxiety.
standards.H-HS.1.3.M: Explain the effects of stress on the body and mind and identify common stressors.
standards.H-HS.1.4.M: Describe bullying, cyberbullying, and harassment, their effects, and the role of bystanders.
standards.H-HS.1.5.M: Identify warning signs of suicide and appropriate ways to seek help for self and others.
standards.H-HS.2.1.M: Analyze how social media, family, peers, and culture influence emotional health and self-image.
standards.H-HS.3.1.M: Identify trusted adults and community resources (including 988) for mental health support.
standards.H-HS.4.1.M: Use effective communication and conflict-resolution skills.
standards.H-HS.5.1.M: Use a decision-making process to address emotional and social challenges.
standards.H-HS.7.1.M: Practice stress management and coping strategies.
standards.H-HS.8.1.M: Advocate for mental health awareness and the reduction of stigma.
standards.H-HS.1.1.A: Explain how alcohol and other drugs affect the developing adolescent brain, including tolerance, dependence, and addiction.
standards.H-HS.1.2.A: Explain the short- and long-term effects of alcohol, cannabis, nicotine/vaping, and other drugs, including fentanyl.
standards.H-HS.1.3.A: Describe the dangers of counterfeit pills and fentanyl, signs of overdose, naloxone use, and California's 911 Good Samaritan law.
standards.H-HS.1.4.A: Explain the legal, social, and economic consequences of substance use, including California laws for minors.
standards.H-HS.2.1.A: Analyze influences such as media, peers, and advertising on substance use.
standards.H-HS.3.2.A: Locate valid information and services for substance use prevention and treatment, including naloxone access.
standards.H-HS.4.2.A: Demonstrate refusal and negotiation skills to avoid substance use.
standards.H-HS.5.1.A: Use a decision-making process to avoid or leave situations involving alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs.
standards.H-HS.8.1.A: Advocate for tobacco-, alcohol-, and drug-free environments.
standards.H-HS.1.1.G: Describe human reproductive anatomy and physiology, puberty, conception, and pregnancy (CA Healthy Youth Act).
standards.H-HS.1.2.G: Describe adolescent development, gender, gender identity, gender expression, and sexual orientation in an inclusive, medically accurate way.
standards.H-HS.1.3.G: Describe characteristics of healthy and unhealthy relationships, consent, and how to prevent dating violence.
standards.H-HS.1.4.G: Explain abstinence and all FDA-approved methods of preventing pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections, including effectiveness.
standards.H-HS.1.5.G: Describe sexually transmitted infections including HIV: transmission, prevention (including PrEP/PEP), testing, and treatment.
standards.H-HS.1.6.G: Explain how to access reproductive and sexual health services and accurate information (CA Healthy Youth Act).
standards.H-HS.1.7.G: Explain pregnancy outcomes and options, the importance of prenatal care, and California's Safely Surrendered Baby Law.
standards.H-HS.1.8.G: Describe sexual harassment, sexual assault, and human trafficking, including prevention strategies and how to seek help.
standards.H-HS.2.1.G: Analyze how media, peers, and culture influence relationships, gender norms, and sexual health decisions.
standards.H-HS.4.1.G: Demonstrate communication skills for setting boundaries, asking for and giving consent, and refusing unwanted pressure.
standards.H-HS.5.1.G: Use a decision-making process to evaluate choices that affect sexual health.
standards.H-HS.1.2.S: Identify ways to reduce the risk of unintentional injuries at home, in water, during recreation and sports, including concussion.
standards.H-HS.1.3.S: Describe causes and prevention of violence, including dating violence, gang violence, and weapons.
standards.H-HS.1.5.S: Describe safe online behavior, including privacy, digital footprint, sextortion, and reporting.
standards.H-HS.1.6.S: Describe emergency preparedness for earthquakes, wildfires, smoke, and other disasters.
standards.H-HS.1.9.S: Describe the procedures for basic first aid, CPR, choking, and use of an AED.
standards.H-HS.5.1.S: Use a decision-making process to evaluate risky situations.
standards.H-HS.7.1.S: Practice injury-prevention behaviors and develop a household emergency plan.
standards.H-HS.8.1.S: Encourage others to adopt safe behaviors.

units.title: Foundations of Wellness and Health Skills
units.big_idea: Health has physical, mental and social sides, and the eight health skills let you protect all three.

units.title: Nutrition and Physical Activity
units.big_idea: Everyday food and movement choices build long-term health, and media messages shape those choices.

units.title: Mental, Emotional and Social Health
units.big_idea: Mental health is health; coping skills, connection and help-seeking keep it strong.

units.title: Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs
units.big_idea: Substances change the developing brain; accurate facts and refusal skills protect your future.

units.title: Healthy Relationships and Sexual Health (CA Healthy Youth Act)
units.big_idea: Medically accurate, inclusive information and strong communication skills support healthy relationships and decisions. Parents/guardians may opt the student out of this unit (Ed. Code 51938); opted-out students complete an alternate project.

units.title: Injury and Violence Prevention and Safety
units.big_idea: Most injuries are predictable and preventable, and prepared people help others in emergencies.

units.title: Personal and Community Health
units.big_idea: Disease prevention, smart health-care use and healthy environments protect individuals and communities.

units.title: Health Advocacy and Personal Wellness Plan
units.big_idea: Health-literate people advocate for themselves and their communities.

objectives: Define health and wellness
Assess personal wellness across physical, mental and social health

days.title: What is health?
days.work: Read the WHO definition of health, then draw and label your own health triangle with three current strengths and one weakness on each side.

days.title: Wellness continuum
days.work: Place 10 scenario cards on a wellness continuum from premature death to high-level wellness and explain each placement in writing.

days.title: Risk and protective factors
days.work: Sort a list of 20 behaviors and conditions into risk factors and protective factors, then identify which you can control.

days.title: Self-assessment
days.work: Complete a 30-question wellness self-inventory and graph your scores by area in your journal.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Write a one-page reflection naming your strongest and weakest areas of health and one reason each matters; take a 10-question vocabulary quiz.

weeks.assessment: Vocabulary quiz and wellness reflection scored on a 4-point rubric.

objectives: Apply a step-by-step decision-making model
Write a SMART health goal

days.title: Values inventory
days.work: Rank 15 personal values (family, honesty, fitness, faith, achievement…) and explain how your top three guide health choices.

days.title: DECIDE model
days.work: Learn the DECIDE steps (Define, Explore, Consider, Identify, Decide, Evaluate) and apply them to a scenario about staying up late before a test.

days.title: Decision practice
days.work: Work through three more scenarios (skipping breakfast, a party invite, a sports injury) with the DECIDE model, writing pros and cons for each option.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Rewrite five vague goals as SMART goals, then write one SMART health goal for yourself with a 6-week tracker.

days.title: Check
days.work: Present your SMART goal and action plan to a parent and complete a short quiz on decision-making steps.

weeks.assessment: Completed DECIDE worksheet and SMART goal action plan.

weeks.topic: Accessing valid health information and services
objectives: Evaluate the credibility of health websites and claims
Identify health care providers and services in the community

days.title: Credible or not?
days.work: Use a CRAAP checklist (Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, Purpose) to evaluate four health websites, including a .gov, a .org and a product site.

days.title: Spotting misinformation
days.work: Analyze three viral social-media health claims and trace each back to (or fail to find) its original research source.

days.title: Health care providers
days.work: Make a chart of health care providers (primary care, specialists, urgent care, ER, school nurse, telehealth) and when to use each.

days.title: Local services map
days.work: Research and list your local clinic, pharmacy, urgent care, Medi-Cal/Covered California options and teen confidential services with phone numbers.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the Unit 1 test on wellness, decision making, goal setting and evaluating health information.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 test and completed local health services directory.

objectives: Describe the six classes of nutrients and their functions
Apply MyPlate recommendations to daily intake

days.title: Six nutrients
days.work: Watch a short nutrition video and make a chart of the six nutrient classes with functions and three food sources each.

days.title: MyPlate
days.work: Use the MyPlate Plan tool to find your personal daily food-group targets and record them.

days.title: Portion lab
days.work: Measure out recommended portions of cereal, rice, juice and nuts with measuring cups and compare them to the amounts you usually serve.

days.title: Food log
days.work: Begin a 3-day food log, recording everything you eat and drink with food groups and approximate portions.

days.title: Check
days.work: Compare your food log to your MyPlate targets and take a 15-question nutrient quiz.

weeks.assessment: Nutrient quiz and food log comparison.

weeks.topic: Food labels and the Dietary Guidelines
objectives: Interpret Nutrition Facts labels and ingredient lists
Compare foods using % Daily Value
materials: 5 packaged food labels from the pantry

days.title: Reading a label
days.work: Annotate a Nutrition Facts label for serving size, calories, %DV, added sugar and sodium using the 5/20 rule.

days.title: Label comparison
days.work: Compare five pantry items in pairs (two cereals, two drinks, etc.) and choose the healthier option with evidence from the labels.

days.title: Sugar and sodium
days.work: Measure the teaspoons of sugar in a can of soda and a sports drink using a sugar bowl and the 4 g = 1 tsp conversion.

days.title: Dietary Guidelines
days.work: Read the Dietary Guidelines for Americans key recommendations and summarize four in your own words.

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete a label-reading practical: answer 10 questions using two unfamiliar food labels.

weeks.assessment: Food-label practical with at least 8/10 correct.

weeks.topic: Energy balance, body image and eating disorders
objectives: Explain energy balance
Recognize warning signs of eating disorders and where to get help

days.title: Energy balance
days.work: Learn how calories in and calories out relate to growth during adolescence and calculate the energy cost of three activities.

days.title: Body image and media
days.work: Compare edited and unedited images from a media-literacy lesson and write about how filtered images affect body image.

days.title: Eating disorders
days.work: Read a KidsHealth article on eating disorders and make a chart of types, warning signs and health effects.

days.title: Diet culture
days.work: Evaluate three fad diets (keto, detox teas, intermittent fasting for teens) for safety and evidence and explain why crash diets backfire.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a letter to a friend showing warning signs, explaining your concern and naming two places to get help; take a short quiz.

weeks.assessment: Supportive letter scored for accurate information and resources; quiz.

weeks.topic: Food marketing, supplements and food safety
objectives: Analyze food marketing techniques
Apply the four steps to food safety

days.title: Marketing techniques
days.work: Analyze three food ads or cereal boxes for techniques (celebrity, health halo, cartoon characters) and identify the target audience.

days.title: Supplements and energy drinks
days.work: Research caffeine content and FDA regulation of supplements and energy drinks and write a consumer warning paragraph.

days.title: Clean, separate, cook, chill
days.work: Learn the four food safety steps and use a food thermometer to check safe internal temperatures while helping cook dinner.

days.title: Kitchen audit
days.work: Audit your home kitchen for food safety (fridge temperature, cutting boards, leftovers dates) and record fixes.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a counter-ad that markets a healthy food using the same persuasive techniques; take a short food-safety quiz.

weeks.topic: Physical activity, sleep and a personal nutrition plan
objectives: Explain the benefits of physical activity and sleep
Build a one-week healthy eating and activity plan

days.title: Activity guidelines
days.work: Learn the 60-minutes-per-day guideline for teens and log your activity minutes and type for today.

days.title: Sleep and health
days.work: Read about teen sleep needs (8–10 hours) and design a sleep-hygiene routine for school nights.

days.title: Meal planning
days.work: Plan three days of balanced meals and snacks on a budget using a grocery flyer and MyPlate targets.

days.title: Cook a meal
days.work: Prepare one meal from your plan with family, photograph it and label its food groups.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the Unit 2 test on nutrients, labels, energy balance, marketing and food safety, and submit your one-week plan.

weeks.assessment: Unit 2 test and personal nutrition/activity plan.

objectives: Describe characteristics of mental wellness
Practice strategies that build resilience

days.title: Mental wellness
days.work: Brainstorm signs of good mental health and compare to a list from a mental health organization.

days.title: Emotions
days.work: Use an emotion wheel to name emotions felt this week and identify body cues for each.

days.title: Self-esteem
days.work: Write a list of 10 personal strengths and ask a family member to add three more.

days.title: Resilience stories
days.work: Read a short biography of someone who overcame adversity and identify the protective factors that helped them.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a reflection describing one setback you faced and the resilience skills you used or could use.

weeks.assessment: Resilience reflection scored with a rubric.

objectives: Explain the stress response
Practice healthy coping strategies

days.title: Stress response
days.work: Diagram the fight-or-flight response and label the hormones and body changes involved.

days.title: Stressor inventory
days.work: List your current stressors, rate each 1–5 and sort them into things you can and cannot control.

days.title: Relaxation practice
days.work: Practice box breathing, progressive muscle relaxation and a 5-4-3-2-1 grounding exercise, rating each afterward.

days.title: Time management
days.work: Build a weekly schedule that balances school, activities, sleep and downtime.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a personal stress-management toolkit card with five strategies and take a short quiz.

objectives: Describe common mental health conditions and treatments
Explain how stigma prevents help-seeking

days.title: Common conditions
days.work: Research anxiety, depression, ADHD and PTSD and complete a chart of symptoms and treatments.

days.title: Myths and facts
days.work: Sort 12 mental health statements into myths and facts and correct each myth.

days.title: Treatment options
days.work: Learn about counseling, therapy types (CBT), medication and support groups.

days.title: Stigma
days.work: Analyze how mental illness is portrayed in a TV show or movie and how that could affect help-seeking.

days.title: Check
days.work: Design an anti-stigma poster with accurate facts and a help resource.

weeks.assessment: Anti-stigma poster scored on accuracy and message.

objectives: Recognize warning signs of suicide
Practice how to get help for self and others

days.title: Warning signs
days.work: Learn the warning signs and risk factors of suicide from a credible prevention source.

days.title: ACT model
days.work: Practice the Acknowledge–Care–Tell steps through role-play scenarios with a parent.

days.title: Resources
days.work: Save 988 and Crisis Text Line (text HOME to 741741) in your phone and list three trusted adults.

days.title: Self-care plan
days.work: Complete a personal safety and support plan with coping strategies and people to contact.

days.title: Check
days.work: Answer scenario questions about how to respond to a friend in crisis.

weeks.assessment: Scenario response check and completed support plan.

objectives: Identify forms of bullying and cyberbullying
Use I-messages and conflict resolution

days.title: Forms of bullying
days.work: Define physical, verbal, relational and cyberbullying and identify CA laws requiring schools to address bullying.

days.title: Social media audit
days.work: Track your screen time for one day and evaluate how each app affects your mood.

days.title: Communication skills
days.work: Practice I-messages and active listening in three role-plays.

days.title: Conflict resolution
days.work: Apply a six-step conflict-resolution model to a family disagreement scenario.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on mental health, stress, help-seeking and communication.

objectives: Explain how drugs affect the brain's reward system
Describe why the teen brain is especially vulnerable

days.title: Reward pathway
days.work: Label a diagram of the brain's reward pathway and explain how dopamine reinforces behavior.

days.title: Teen brain
days.work: Read NIDA materials on adolescent brain development and summarize why the prefrontal cortex matters.

days.title: Tolerance and dependence
days.work: Create a flowchart showing the progression from use to tolerance, dependence and addiction.

days.title: Addiction as disease
days.work: Discuss how genetics, environment and early use affect addiction risk.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write an explanation of addiction for a younger student and take a short quiz.

objectives: Describe the health effects of nicotine and vaping
Analyze tobacco marketing to teens

days.title: Nicotine effects
days.work: Research short- and long-term health effects of nicotine and vaping, including lung injury.

days.title: What's in a vape?
days.work: Analyze an ingredient list of e-cigarette aerosol and identify harmful chemicals.

days.title: Marketing to teens
days.work: Analyze vape and tobacco ads for techniques targeting youth (flavors, design, influencers).

days.title: California laws
days.work: Learn California's Tobacco 21 law and flavored tobacco ban; research quitting resources (Kick It California).

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a counter-marketing social media post on vaping and take a short quiz.

objectives: Explain how alcohol affects the body
Analyze alcohol's role in injuries and violence

days.title: Alcohol and the body
days.work: Trace alcohol's path through the body and describe effects on each organ system.

days.title: BAC factors
days.work: Learn what affects blood alcohol concentration and why 'sobering up' cannot be sped up.

days.title: Alcohol poisoning
days.work: Learn the signs of alcohol poisoning and the steps to take, including calling 911.

days.title: Laws and consequences
days.work: Research California's zero-tolerance law for drivers under 21 and other legal consequences.

days.title: Check
days.work: Use the decision-making model on a party scenario involving alcohol and take a short quiz.

weeks.topic: Cannabis, prescription drugs, fentanyl and naloxone
objectives: Describe effects of cannabis and prescription misuse
Recognize opioid overdose and how to respond

days.title: Cannabis
days.work: Research cannabis effects on memory, motivation and mental health, including high-potency products.

days.title: Prescription misuse
days.work: Learn why sharing or misusing prescription drugs is dangerous, and how to dispose of medicine safely.

days.title: Fentanyl
days.work: Learn about fentanyl, counterfeit pills and why 'one pill can kill', using CDPH/DEA materials.

days.title: Overdose response
days.work: Learn overdose signs and practice the steps for giving naloxone (Narcan) using a training video and checklist.

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete a scenario quiz on recognizing and responding to an overdose.

weeks.topic: Influences, refusal skills and semester review
objectives: Analyze influences on substance use
Demonstrate refusal skills

days.title: Influences
days.work: Map the influences on teen substance use (peers, family, media, community) and identify protective factors.

days.title: Refusal skills
days.work: Practice five refusal strategies (say no, give a reason, suggest an alternative, leave, use humor) in role-plays.

days.title: Advocacy
days.work: Create a short PSA promoting a substance-free lifestyle.

days.title: Semester review
days.work: Review units 1–4 using a study guide and practice questions.

days.title: Semester exam
days.work: Take the semester exam covering wellness, nutrition, mental health and substance use.

weeks.assessment: Semester exam and refusal-skills role-play checklist.

objectives: Identify characteristics of healthy and unhealthy relationships
Practice asking for and giving consent

days.title: Unit introduction
days.work: Parent reviews the CA Healthy Youth Act notice and opt-out option (Ed. Code 51938); student discusses family values and expectations for the unit.

days.title: Healthy vs. unhealthy
days.work: Sort relationship behaviors on a continuum from healthy to abusive and identify red flags.

days.title: Consent
days.work: Learn what affirmative consent means under California law and analyze scenarios for whether consent was given.

days.title: Boundaries
days.work: Write examples of personal boundaries and practice communicating them clearly.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a short analysis of a fictional relationship using what you learned; quiz.

objectives: Describe reproductive anatomy and physiology
Explain changes during adolescence

days.title: Endocrine system
days.work: Learn how hormones drive puberty and label the endocrine glands.

days.title: Female anatomy
days.work: Label female reproductive anatomy and describe the menstrual cycle.

days.title: Male anatomy
days.work: Label male reproductive anatomy and describe its functions.

days.title: Self-care
days.work: Learn about reproductive health exams, hygiene and when to see a doctor.

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete an anatomy labeling quiz on both reproductive systems and explain the menstrual cycle phases in a short written response.

weeks.topic: Gender identity, sexual orientation and respect
objectives: Describe gender identity and sexual orientation accurately
Analyze media influences on gender norms

days.title: Key terms
days.work: Learn medically accurate definitions of sex, gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation.

days.title: Gender norms
days.work: Analyze gender stereotypes in ads and media and how they affect relationships.

days.title: Respect and inclusion
days.work: Discuss how to treat all people with respect and identify school anti-discrimination protections.

days.title: Media and relationships
days.work: Analyze how movies and music portray relationships and compare to healthy relationship traits.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a reflection on how media influences relationship expectations.

objectives: Describe conception, fetal development and prenatal care
Explain pregnancy options and the Safely Surrendered Baby Law

days.title: Conception
days.work: Describe fertilization and implantation with a diagram.

days.title: Fetal development
days.work: Create an illustrated timeline of embryonic and fetal development by trimester, noting when major organs form and why early prenatal care matters.

days.title: Prenatal care
days.work: Research prenatal care and how substances affect fetal development.

days.title: Options and laws
days.work: Learn about parenting, adoption and abortion as legal options, and California's Safely Surrendered Baby Law.

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete a budget activity estimating first-year costs of raising a baby, and a quiz.

objectives: Explain abstinence and contraceptive methods
Compare effectiveness of methods

days.title: Abstinence
days.work: Discuss abstinence as the only 100% effective method and reasons people choose it.

days.title: Contraceptive methods
days.work: Learn about all FDA-approved methods using a CDC effectiveness chart.

days.title: Comparing methods
days.work: Compare methods by effectiveness, STI protection and access.

days.title: Decisions
days.work: Apply the decision-making model to a scenario about sexual health choices.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a quiz matching methods to typical-use effectiveness and STI protection, and write which methods protect against both pregnancy and STIs.

objectives: Describe STI transmission, symptoms, testing and treatment
Explain HIV prevention including PrEP and PEP

days.title: Common STIs
days.work: Research chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, HPV and herpes: symptoms, testing and treatment.

days.title: HIV
days.work: Learn how HIV attacks the immune system and how it is and isn't transmitted.

days.title: Prevention
days.work: Learn prevention methods including abstinence, condoms, HPV vaccine, PrEP and PEP.

days.title: Testing and services
days.work: Locate confidential testing services for teens in California using the CDC GetTested locator.

days.title: Check
days.work: Finish an STI fact chart (cause, symptoms, curable or treatable, prevention, testing) for six infections and take a 15-question quiz.

weeks.topic: Sexual violence, trafficking and accessing services
objectives: Recognize sexual harassment, assault and trafficking
Identify how to get help

days.title: Harassment and assault
days.work: Define sexual harassment and assault and learn your rights under Title IX.

days.title: Human trafficking
days.work: Learn how traffickers recruit teens online and in person, and warning signs.

days.title: Getting help
days.work: Identify hotlines (RAINN, National Human Trafficking Hotline) and trusted adults.

days.title: Minor consent
days.work: Learn which health services California minors can access confidentially.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Take the Unit 5 test; opted-out students submit their alternate project.

weeks.topic: Unintentional injuries: home, water, sports and concussion
objectives: Identify causes of common unintentional injuries
Explain concussion signs and return-to-play rules

days.title: Injury data
days.work: Analyze CDC data on leading causes of teen injury and death.

days.title: Home safety
days.work: Complete a home safety audit for falls, fire, poisoning and firearms storage.

days.title: Water safety
days.work: Watch a video on what drowning really looks like, list the signs, and write water safety rules for pools, rivers and the ocean (rip currents).

days.title: Concussion
days.work: Learn concussion signs and California's return-to-play law (AB 2127).

days.title: Check
days.work: Present your home safety audit to family with the three highest-priority fixes and complete one fix (e.g., test smoke alarms, lock up medicines).

objectives: Describe causes and prevention of violence
Identify warning signs of dating violence

days.title: Causes of violence
days.work: Identify risk factors and protective factors for violence.

days.title: De-escalation
days.work: Practice de-escalation techniques (calm voice, space, active listening, walking away) in three role-plays and rate which worked best.

days.title: Dating violence
days.work: Learn the cycle of abuse and warning signs using loveisrespect.org.

days.title: Weapons and gangs
days.work: Discuss the dangers of weapons and gang involvement and how to report threats.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a safety plan for a scenario involving dating violence.

objectives: Describe risks online including sextortion
Protect privacy and digital footprint

days.title: Digital footprint
days.work: Search your own name and review what's public; adjust privacy settings.

days.title: Sextortion
days.work: Learn what sextortion is and how to get help (Take It Down, NCMEC).

days.title: Online predators
days.work: Analyze a case study of online grooming, list the tactics used at each stage, and practice blocking and reporting on two apps you use.

days.title: Digital wellness
days.work: Create a personal tech-use plan with phone-free times, notification settings and a bedtime device rule, and share it with a parent.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a digital safety scenario quiz (phishing message, sextortion threat, oversharing post) explaining the safest response for each.

weeks.topic: Emergency preparedness: earthquakes, wildfires and smoke
objectives: Prepare for natural disasters common in California
Build a household emergency plan

days.title: Earthquakes
days.work: Practice Drop, Cover and Hold On and identify safe spots at home.

days.title: Wildfire and smoke
days.work: Learn evacuation steps and how to read the Air Quality Index.

days.title: Go-bag
days.work: Using the Ready.gov list, write a go-bag checklist for your household and gather water, flashlight, medications, N95 masks and copies of documents.

days.title: Family plan
days.work: Create a family emergency plan with meeting points and contacts.

days.title: Check
days.work: Present your family emergency plan, run a timed earthquake and evacuation drill, and record what to improve.

weeks.topic: Basic first aid and Hands-Only CPR
objectives: Describe basic first aid
Demonstrate Hands-Only CPR

days.title: Emergency steps
days.work: Learn the Check–Call–Care steps and practice a mock 911 call giving location, situation and number of victims.

days.title: Bleeding and burns
days.work: Practice treating cuts and burns using a first aid kit.

days.title: Hands-Only CPR
days.work: Practice Hands-Only CPR on a pillow to the beat of 'Stayin' Alive'.

days.title: AED
days.work: Watch an AED demonstration video, then sequence the AED steps on cards and talk through pad placement on a diagram.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Take the Unit 6 test and perform a 2-minute Hands-Only CPR skills check for a parent with a checklist.

weeks.assessment: Unit 6 test and CPR skills check.

objectives: Explain how pathogens spread
Describe how vaccines work
materials: glitter or lotion for handwashing demo

days.title: Pathogens
days.work: Compare bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites with examples of diseases.

days.title: Transmission
days.work: Do a glitter handwashing experiment to show how germs spread.

days.title: Immune system
days.work: Diagram the immune response and how vaccines train immunity.

days.title: Vaccines
days.work: Review the California school immunization schedule and teen vaccines (Tdap, HPV, meningococcal, flu).

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a quiz on communicable diseases and write a paragraph explaining herd immunity using a classroom-sized example.

weeks.topic: Chronic diseases and personal health care
objectives: Identify risk factors for chronic disease
Practice personal health habits

days.title: Chronic diseases
days.work: Research heart disease, type 2 diabetes and cancer risk factors.

days.title: Family history
days.work: Interview a family member to build a family health history.

days.title: Prevention
days.work: Make a chart of recommended screenings (blood pressure, cholesterol, skin checks, Pap/HPV, testicular self-exam) and the lifestyle habits that lower chronic-disease risk.

days.title: Personal care
days.work: Learn about dental care, vision, hearing protection and sun safety.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a personal chronic-disease prevention plan using your family history, with three habits to start now and screenings to ask about later.

weeks.topic: Consumer health and the health care system
objectives: Evaluate health products and services
Understand health insurance basics

days.title: Advertising claims
days.work: Evaluate three health product ads (supplement, acne cream, fitness gadget) for claims, evidence and red flags of quackery.

days.title: Health insurance
days.work: Learn insurance terms and how Medi-Cal and Covered California work.

days.title: Medications
days.work: Compare brand-name vs. generic drugs and read an OTC drug label.

days.title: Being a patient
days.work: Prepare a list of questions and a medication/allergy list for a doctor visit, then role-play checking in and describing symptoms.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a consumer health quiz on insurance terms, OTC labels and evaluating claims, including calculating a cost with a deductible and copay.

objectives: Explain how the environment affects health
Identify community health resources

days.title: Air quality
days.work: Check local AQI and research health effects of air pollution.

days.title: Water quality
days.work: Find your water supplier's Consumer Confidence Report, identify your water source and two contaminants tested, and compare to legal limits.

days.title: Environmental justice
days.work: Learn how pollution affects communities differently using CalEnviroScreen.

days.title: Public health
days.work: Research the role of the county public health department.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on communicable and chronic disease, consumer health and environmental health.

objectives: Choose a health issue and advocate for change
Create an advocacy product

days.title: Choose a topic
days.work: Choose a teen health issue from the course (e.g., vaping, sleep, teen mental health access, wildfire smoke) and write a one-paragraph problem statement with a target audience.

days.title: Research
days.work: Gather three credible sources (.gov, .edu, peer-reviewed) and record two statistics and one expert recommendation on a note sheet with citations.

days.title: Create
days.work: Build an advocacy product: a 60-second PSA video, an infographic poster, or a letter to a school board member or legislator with a clear call to action.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Get feedback from a parent using the advocacy rubric (accuracy, audience, persuasive appeal, call to action) and revise the product.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the advocacy product to family or a co-op group, answer questions, and submit it with a works-cited list.

weeks.topic: Final review and personal wellness plan
objectives: Review course content
Write a personal wellness plan

days.title: Review: units 1–4
days.work: Complete a review grid for wellness, nutrition, mental health and substance use, then quiz yourself with 30 flashcards built from unit vocabulary.

days.title: Review: units 5–7
days.work: Answer 25 practice questions on relationships, injury prevention, disease prevention and consumer health, and correct missed items with notes.

days.title: Wellness plan
days.work: Write a personal wellness plan with one SMART goal each for physical, mental/emotional and social health, including supports, obstacles and a tracking method.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the cumulative final exam (multiple choice, scenarios and a short decision-making essay).

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Compare your week-1 wellness self-inventory to a retake today and write a one-page reflection on how your health knowledge and habits changed.
